main_issue: Whether and when Agent D may cook strong-smelling sambal in the shared kitchen, given the smell affects the living room, bedrooms and laundry

A-B.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling cooking (T1) and B proposed a heads-up (T2). B then backed weekends or late nights (T6), A accepted Tue/Thu/weekend (T10) and B agreed (T12).

A-C.evidence: C objected that late nights still hit the laundry (T8). A accepted D's Tue/Thu/weekend plan (T10) and C also agreed (T14).

A-D.evidence: A wanted no strong-smelling cooking and then asked for late-night or weekend sambal (T5). D offered Tue/Thu/weekend (T9), A said 'that works for me' (T10) and D replied 'Okay, great' (T15).

B-C.evidence: B suggested a heads-up, C said the yard still gets the smell (T3), B accepted weekends or late nights (T6). Both later agreed to D's plan (T12, T14).

B-D.evidence: B proposed a heads-up (T2) and backed weekends or late nights (T6). D offered Tue/Thu/weekend (T9), B said it works (T12) and D replied 'Okay, great' (T15).

C-D.evidence: C said late-night weekday cooking harms Mon/Wed/Fri laundry (T8). D excluded those nights (T9), C accepted (T14), and D confirmed (T19).
